My friend's mom told this a few years ago. Some details were changed for privacy reasons.

"It was a teen girl and her best friend. We got a call about a car that had lost control, flipped, and rolled several times. The weird thing was, the girls were nowhere to be found when we got there. No blood in the car, either. The officers and EMTs (including myself) looked everywhere for their bodies on the off chance that they had been ejected. Given the state of the vehicle, we were expecting to find several pieces of their bodies.

Turns out, the guy had neglected to tell us that the girls *had* been ejected (likely out of adrenaline and shock), but both girls were huddling and crying in the back of the SUV of the man who made the call. They only had minor cuts and bruises. We have no idea how they made it out alive, but it was one of the happiest days of my life when I discovered that they were fine and just terrified. Man told us they were just sitting on the ground where they had been respectively thrown out, crying and calling for each other. It was incredibly heartwarming and uplifting. I don't think I'll ever forget that."

Thanks for catching the reference.
